title: require()
summary: Loads a ModuleScript and returns whatever value the module returns. Modules run once; every later require gets the same cached value.

parameters.name: moduleScript
parameters.description: The ModuleScript instance to load. A string in the form `"path"` with asset IDs is supported for published modules.

reference.returns: Whatever the module's top-level `return` produced. If the module returns nothing, require gives `true`. If it errors, the error propagates to the caller.

details.heading: Runs once, cached forever
details.body: The first `require()` executes the module's code and stores the result. Every later require — from any script on that runtime (client or server) — returns the cached value without re-running the module.

details.heading: Client and server cache separately
details.body: The client's require cache and the server's are independent. A module required on both sides runs once per side.

details.heading: Yielding
details.body: If the module's code yields (task.wait etc.), the requiring thread yields with it. Circular requires error instead of deadlocking.

details.heading: Access rules
details.body: You can only require ModuleScripts the current runtime can read: clients can't require modules in ServerScriptService/ServerStorage.

explanation.whatItIs: The bridge between scripts. `require()` runs a ModuleScript (if it hasn't run yet) and hands you whatever that module returned — usually a table of functions.
explanation.whyItExists: One giant script per game is unmaintainable. require lets you split code into focused modules and share them everywhere: shared utilities, state stores, service wrappers.
whenToUse: Singletons: a module that returns a state object becomes a shared instance
Organizing large projects into folders of modules
whenNotToUse: Don't require a ModuleScript expecting a *fresh copy* each time — it's cached; clone the module first if you truly need isolation
Don't use require as a general 'run this script' tool — Scripts/LocalScripts have their own runtime
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
ModuleScript
     ↓
require()
     ↓
module runs / loads        (first time only)
     ↓
return value
     ↓
your variable receives it   (every require: same value)
```
tips: Cache services inside modules: `local Players = game:GetService("Players")` at the top
Return a table of functions for a namespace-style API: `Module.DoThing()`
If require() returns true, the module forgot its `return`
commonMistakes: Forgetting the module's `return` — require then gives `true`
Expecting module code to run again per require — it runs once
Circular requires: module A requires B, B requires A → error
Requiring from a place that can't access the module (client requiring a ServerStorage module)

examples.title: Standard module usage
examples.code:
-- == ReplicatedStorage/CoinUtils (ModuleScript) ==
local CoinUtils = {}

function CoinUtils.spawnAt(position)
    local coin = Instance.new("Part")
    coin.Name = "Coin"
    coin.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
    coin.Position = position
    coin.Parent = workspace
    return coin
end

return CoinUtils

-- == Any Script or LocalScript ==
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local CoinUtils = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("CoinUtils"))

CoinUtils.spawnAt(Vector3.new(0, 5, 0))
examples.whyItWorks: require runs CoinUtils once, gets the returned table, and every script that requires it shares that same table.

examples.title: Module as a singleton store
examples.code:
-- == GameState (ModuleScript) ==
local GameState = {
    phase = "Lobby",
    round = 0,
}
return GameState

-- Anywhere, client or server (each side gets its own copy):
local GameState = require(script.Parent.GameState)
GameState.phase = "Playing"   -- visible to every requirer on this side
